newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court tells states to recognize each others' benefit awards.
newsitem.headline: Court tells states to recognize each others' benefit awards.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday Community rules governing unemployment benefits for frontier workers require member states to recognize unemployment benefits paid by another member state.
A Dutch national living in Belgium and working in the Netherlands lost her job and went on unemployment in Belgium. When she moved back to the Netherlands, she sought unemployment benefits there.
The Dutch authority denied her claims, declaring her ineligible for "follow-on benefits" because she had not received her original unemployment benefits in the Netherlands.

"It follows that where an unemployed frontier worker, after receiving unemployment benefit in the state in which he is resident, settles in the member state in which he was last employed...the state in which he was last employed must begin ...to assume its obligations in relation to unemployment benefit," the court said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Dutch)
"Social security - Wholly unemployed frontier worker - Unemployment benefits in the competentmember state - Regulation (EEC) No 1408/71"
Reference from the Raad van State (Netherlands) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
Commissie voor de Behandeling van Administratieve Geschillen ingevolge Atikel 41 der Algemene Bijstandswet inde Provincie Noord-Brabant

on the interpretation of article 67 of Council regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 of 14 June 1971 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to self-employed persons and to members of their families moving within the Community, as amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83 of 2 June 1983 (OJ 1983 L 230, p.6) and article 6 of the EC treaty

The provisions of Council regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 of 14 June 1971 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to self-employed persons and to members of their families moving within the Community, as amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83 of 2 June 1983 relating to unemployment benefits, and in particular article 71(1)(a)(ii), read in conjunction with article 13, are to be interpreted as meaning that where, in the state of last employment, the grant of an allowance following on from an unemployment benefit is made subject to the conditon that the frontier worker concerned has received unemployment benefit for a given period, that state is required to take into account unemployment benefit received by that worker in the state in which he resides in accordance with article 71(1)(a)(ii), as though that benefit had been received in the former state.
